strategic_issues: India accuses Pakistan of sponsoring cross-border terrorism
Indus Waters Treaty suspended by India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack
Pakistan's deepening defence partnerships with China, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia
trade_dependencies: Formal bilateral trade is minimal and has been suspended for extended periods amid political tension

energy_relationship.notes: No significant direct energy trade between the two countries

military_relationship.posture: high alert following the May 2025 conflict
military_relationship.notes: On 22 April 2025, gunmen killed 26 people near Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir; India blamed Pakistan-linked militants. India launched 'Operation Sindoor' on 7 May 2025, striking targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Four days of strikes and counter-strikes followed (informally called the '87/88-hour war' by some analysts) before a ceasefire was announced on 10 May 2025. India has stated the ceasefire was negotiated directly between the two militaries; the US publicly described it as US-brokered, a characterization India has downplayed. Indian officials (e.g. Vice Admiral K. Swaminathan, Dec 2025) said the threat of Indian naval offensive action was a key factor in Pakistan requesting the ceasefire.
military_relationship.reported_chinese_pakistani_cooperation: China has acknowledged its aviation industry provided technical assistance to Pakistan during the conflict, per Chinese and Indian reporting. Indian and Pakistani sources dispute aircraft-loss figures from the engagement; neither government has released full official confirmation.
military_relationship.recent_activity_aug_2026: Indian outlets (Organiser, Sunday Guardian Live, India.com, Tribune India — 20-21 Aug 2026) reported a roughly 60-hour surge of Chinese and Turkish military transport aircraft landing at Pakistani airbases (Nur Khan, Masroor), which Indian security sources interpreted as a possible arms/equipment resupply, ahead of SCO and BRICS meetings. The exact cargo has not been officially confirmed by China, Turkey, or Pakistan.

diplomatic_relationship.notes: India's Ministry of External Affairs has publicly urged Turkey to press Pakistan on cross-border terrorism, citing an estimated 350+ Turkish-linked drones and reported Turkish operational assistance to Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict (per Indian government and Tribune India reporting).

major_disputes: Siachen and Sir Creek boundary disagreements
areas_of_cooperation: Limited — occasional back-channel and multilateral (SCO) engagement only
escalation_factors: Further militant attacks attributed to Pakistan-based groups
Continued Chinese and Turkish arms resupply to Pakistan (reported Aug 2026 airlift)
New Pakistan-Turkey-Saudi Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (7 Aug 2026), which commits the three states to treat an attack on one as an attack on all
deescalation_factors: The May 2025 ceasefire has broadly held despite mutual accusations of violations
International (particularly US) interest in avoiding renewed conflict between two nuclear powers
